call_points.text: MF licence final inspection done; SIF launch expected after the licence, with the long-short strategy to migrate into it.
RTA and trusteeship services expected to go live by middle of Q3; currently at 22% of chosen segments.
FY27 will carry incremental asset management costs for new strategies and the MF/SIF build.
ECM pipeline has 40-45 live mandates; Q4 deals were pushed and recovery is expected in coming quarters.
RBI bank guarantee norms cost about ₹10-15 Cr a year net of deposit costs; ROCE impact called negligible.
Asset services yields held despite a 50 bps rate cut; a rate reversal would lift yields as deposits reprice.
PAG, a holder for about 5 years, will exit at some point but no process is currently on.
Mutual fund commission cut from April has hardly any impact; MF is under 20% of IE revenues.

operating_notes.text: Total firm-level client assets were ₹4.5 lakh Cr at FY26, with a mark-to-market impact on the headline number.
Nuvama Private ARR assets about ₹54,000 Cr with yields of 0.85-1% (1% this quarter), guided to average 90-95 bps.
Nuvama Wealth MPIS assets about ₹39,000 Cr with ₹8,900 Cr net new money in FY26, 30% of opening assets.
Lending book crossed ₹5,000 Cr with NII growth of about 12% QoQ, at 20-22% of segment revenue.
ARR yield was 82 bps in Q1 versus about 90 bps last year, guided at 80-90 bps near term.
Offshore revenue contribution guided at 5-7% this year; Dubai has broken even.
Nuvama Asset Management received SEBI approval to establish a Specialized Investment Fund (SIF) under SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026.

timeline.summary: Nuvama Wealth subsidiary NWIL received a ₹8.70 lakh penalty from NSE regarding operational inspection observations.
On May 6, 2026, SEBI issued an administrative warning to Nuvama Wealth's subsidiary NWIL regarding inspection observations.
Nuvama Wealth Management Limited hosted earnings conference call recording for Q4-FY25-26 on May 12, 2026, available at provided link.

Nuvama's Q4/FY26 earnings call (May 12, 2026) guided FY27 fund targets of ₹1,000-1,500 Cr for private equity fund 4, about ₹1,500 Cr for a first private credit fund and ₹3,000-4,000 Cr for the next commercial real estate fund, with the MF licence pending.
Q1FY27 (Jul 31, 2026 call): revenue ₹909 Cr (+18% YoY), PAT above ₹300 Cr, client assets ₹5,36,000 Cr; CRISIL upgraded to AA stable.
On 19 October 2026, Nuvama Wealth Management announced that its subsidiary Nuvama Asset Management received SEBI approval to establish a Specialized Investment Fund.
